title: Graph Linear Inequalities
student_objective: I can graph a two-variable linear inequality using the correct boundary line and shaded solution region.

concept_cards.title: Graph the boundary first
concept_cards.content: Replace the inequality symbol with = and graph the boundary line.

concept_cards.title: Solid or dashed?
concept_cards.content: Use a solid line for ≤ or ≥ because equality is included. Use a dashed line for < or > because equality is excluded.

concept_cards.title: Use a test point
concept_cards.content: Test a convenient point such as (0,0) when it is not on the boundary. If the point makes the inequality true, shade the side containing that point.

concept_cards.title: The shaded region is the answer
concept_cards.content: Every point in the shaded half-plane satisfies the inequality. The boundary is included only when the line is solid.

boundary_style.teacher_signal: Student confuses solid and dashed boundaries.

solve_for_y.teacher_signal: Student changes direction incorrectly when dividing by a negative.

items.prompt: Should y<2x+3 use a solid or dashed boundary line?
items.tutor_behavior: Connect strict inequalities with excluded boundary points.
hint_steps: Strict inequalities exclude points on the boundary.

items.prompt: Does the point (0,0) satisfy y≥x-2? Answer yes or no.
items.tutor_behavior: Substitute the test point into the inequality.
Model boundary style and shading direction together.
hint_steps: Graph y=-x+4 as a solid line.
Because y is less than or equal, shade below the line.

solution_steps.explanation: The inequality asks for y-values less than the boundary.

items.tutor_behavior: Use the sign in y-form to read shading directly.
hint_steps: Graph y=3x-1 with a dashed line.
Shade above because y is greater than the boundary.

solution_steps.explanation: Greater y-values lie above the line.

items.prompt: For y≥2x+1, give the boundary style and shading direction.

solution_steps.explanation: y is greater than the line's y-value.

items.prompt: For y<-2x+5, give the boundary style and shading direction.
Rewrite 2x+y>6 in y-form and state how to graph it.
items.tutor_behavior: Isolate y before reading the graph behavior.
hint_steps: Use a dashed line and shade above.

solution_steps.explanation: The inequality is strict and y is greater.

items.prompt: For y≤4x-7, state boundary style and shading direction.
items.tutor_behavior: Student applies the graphing rule independently.

items.prompt: For y>-x-3, state boundary style and shading direction.
items.tutor_behavior: Student applies strict inequality and shading.

items.prompt: Rewrite -2y≤4x+8 in y-form and state how to graph it.
items.tutor_behavior: Emphasize inequality reversal when dividing by -2.
hint_steps: y≥-2x-4, so use a solid line and shade above.

solution_steps.explanation: Divide by -2 and reverse the inequality.
Equality is included and y is greater.

items.prompt: For y≥-3x+2, state boundary style and shading direction.
items.tutor_behavior: Mastery check on core graph rule.

items.prompt: For y<5x+1, state boundary style and shading direction.
Does (0,0) satisfy y≤2x+4? Answer yes or no.
items.tutor_behavior: Use a test point to verify shading.
hint_steps: The statement is true, so yes.

items.prompt: Rewrite 3x-2y>8 in y-form and state how to graph it.
items.tutor_behavior: Reinforce reversal when dividing by a negative coefficient.
hint_steps: y<(3/2)x-4; use dashed and shade below.

solution_steps.explanation: Divide by -2 and reverse the sign.

items.prompt: Which boundary style is used for x+y=5 when it is the boundary of x+y≤5?
items.tutor_behavior: Connect equality inclusion to the boundary.
